_comment: #892 Phase 3 — the inverse of any workflow's `changes` filter table. `skipped` counts as a PASS in a rolled-up required `check`, which makes such a table load-bearing: a path no filter names wakes no path-gated lane and merges green, unexercised (#890 W0 fixed one instance of exactly this by hand). No workflow carries a filter table today — gate.yml, the one pull-request entry point, is unfiltered by ruling (#1020) — so every entry here names the ALWAYS-ON job that covers the path. scripts/lint-path-filters.mjs requires every workspace package and every tracked top-level directory to be claimed by a filter OR to appear here. An entry naming a path that no longer exists fails as stale — a dead exemption reads like a reviewed decision and is not one.

alwaysOn.assets: Product icon sources (13 files: the .svg masters plus the generated .icns/.ico/.png). They are consumed at PACKAGING time by lane-release-desktop.yml and lane-release-mobile.yml, not by any PR lane — there is no per-PR claim about them to gate, and the release lanes rebuild from them unconditionally on every tag.
alwaysOn.packages/test-kit: Test-only harness (no product surface, not shipped in any artifact). Covered by gate.yml's `ts-static` step (`cargo xtask gate --profile pr` runs `bun run check:push:static`: format check, oxlint over the whole tree, turbo lint and typecheck over the affected workspaces) on every PR, UNFILTERED. Its three consumers are packages/design's own tests, which import its fake clock.
alwaysOn.contracts: The v1 tree's language-neutral fixtures and ledgers (#1020). Covered by gate.yml — `cargo xtask gate --profile pr` on every PR, UNFILTERED, by ruling: the v1 gate is one command with one step list and no `paths:` table at all, so there is no lane to wake selectively and nothing for ci.yml's filter table to claim.
alwaysOn.crates: The v1 Rust workspace (#1020). Covered by gate.yml — `cargo xtask gate --profile pr` on every PR, UNFILTERED, for the same reason as `contracts` above: `cargo fmt/clippy/test --workspace` and the structural rules see the whole tree on every run, and the nightly profile adds the v0 oracle on top of it.
alwaysOn.receipts: The audit trail itself. Covered by `governance.yml` (unfiltered, runs .governance/run.sh on every PR) which owns receipt-per-issue, commit-issue-receipt-match and doc-integrity. A receipt change has no product lane to wake.
alwaysOn.desktop: The v1 desktop seat (#1020 wave 3 lane F): Electron main, the renderer, and the Playwright run. Covered by gate.yml — `cargo xtask gate --profile pr` runs `desktop-unit` (the vitest project over desktop/ and extension/, plus the three tsconfigs) on every PR, UNFILTERED, for the same reason as `crates` and `contracts` above: the v1 gate is one command with one step list and no `paths:` table, so there is no lane to wake selectively. The `desktop-e2e` step — a real Electron app over a real sidecar, which is the lane's exit criterion — is in the nightly profile because it builds a binary and launches a browser; see contracts/handoff/F/desktop-e2e.md for why that split is where it is.
alwaysOn.extension: The v1 browser Companion (#1020 wave 3 lane F, finished in wave 4 lane extension): MV3 over native messaging, no network and no WASM. Its pure layer is in the SAME vitest project as desktop/ — one more consumer of the same seat socket — so `desktop-unit` in gate.yml's `pr` profile covers it on every PR, UNFILTERED, and `extension-unit` adds the two type programs and the Companion's own lint (the manifests against contracts/extension/ids.json, and every method name against the eighteen). The `extension-e2e` step — Chromium loading the unpacked build over a real native port — is in the nightly profile because an extension needs a full Chromium and therefore a display.
alwaysOn.copy: The v1 copy leaves (#1020 wave 4): one `copy/<app>.json` per app, emitted from each blueprint's `*-copy.ts` by contracts/tools/export-copy.ts and read by the mobile shell. Covered by gate.yml — `cargo xtask gate --profile pr` on every PR, UNFILTERED — whose `emitters` step re-runs the emitter, formats, and asserts `git diff --exit-code -- copy design mobile`, so a leaf that moved without its artifact is red on the run that moved it.
alwaysOn.design: The v1 design corpus (#1020 waves 3-4): `identity-corpus.json` and `native-theme.json`, both generated from `packages/design` by contracts/tools/export-design-corpus.ts and export-native-theme.ts. Covered by gate.yml's `emitters` step on every PR, UNFILTERED, exactly as `copy` above — the two are one assertion. `packages/design` itself has its own entry; this one is about the generated tree those emitters write.
alwaysOn.mobile: The v1 KMP mobile shell (#1020 wave 3 lane E). Two halves, and only one is affordable per PR. Covered on every PR by gate.yml, UNFILTERED: `rules` runs `commonmain-no-platform-import` over every `commonMain` source, and `emitters` regenerates `mobile/shared/.../Copy.kt` and asserts the tree is clean. The JVM round trip and the Gradle build are `cargo xtask gate --profile mobile-jvm`, a separate job in gate-nightly.yml — a second toolchain with its own 420 s cold ledger row, which #1020 ruled off the per-PR loop in D-1020-B2-3. The nightly latency on that half is the decision, stated rather than hidden behind a skip.
alwaysOn.packages/design: The design system every seat lowers from. Covered on every PR, UNFILTERED, by gate.yml: `emitters` regenerates `design/` and `mobile/`'s theme from it and asserts the tree is clean, and `ts-static` step (`cargo xtask gate --profile pr` runs `bun run check:push:static`: format check, oxlint over the whole tree, turbo lint and typecheck over the affected workspaces) on every PR, UNFILTERED.
alwaysOn.scripts: Repository tooling. Covered by gate.yml on every PR, UNFILTERED: `ci-policy` runs `lint:workflow-pins`, `lint:ci-egress` and `lint:path-filters` from here, and `ts-static` step (`cargo xtask gate --profile pr` runs `bun run check:push:static`: format check, oxlint over the whole tree, turbo lint and typecheck over the affected workspaces) on every PR, UNFILTERED. The rest of the tree's contract bundle (`lint:product`) runs on the merged tree in candidate.yml's `rung1-on-main`.
alwaysOn.tests: The JSON ledgers under tests/ (floors, budgets, inventory, quarantine, claims, journeys and this file). Covered by gate.yml on every PR, UNFILTERED: `ci-policy` reads this file through `lint:path-filters`, and `ts-static`'s format check holds every ledger's bytes. Their ratchets (`lint:ledgers`, `lint:journey-ledger`) run in candidate.yml's `rung1-on-main` on the merged tree.
alwaysOn.docs: Prose. Covered by `governance.yml` (unfiltered, runs .governance/run.sh on every PR), whose `law` directive owns doc-integrity — every link and anchor in a doc resolves. A doc change has no product lane to wake.
alwaysOn.deploy: The v1 deploy tree (#1020): the gateway Dockerfile, the VPS installer and the systemd/launchd units. Covered on every PR, UNFILTERED, only by gate.yml's `secrets` step (gitleaks over the working tree): nothing here compiles, and the one behavioural check — `vps-smoke`, which stages deploy/vps/install.sh — runs in the `release` profile against a built binary, which is where an installer can first be exercised.
alwaysOn.centraid-city: The standalone Three.js site bundled into the public docs by `bun run docs:bundle`; it has its own lockfile and is not a root workspace. Covered by gate.yml's `ts-static` step (`cargo xtask gate --profile pr` runs `bun run check:push:static`: format check, oxlint over the whole tree, turbo lint and typecheck over the affected workspaces) on every PR, UNFILTERED — the format check and oxlint see its sources. Its own `tsc` and Vite build run only when the docs site is bundled.
